header:
Date: 2026-12-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Gomez (Redwood Product), Sara Martinez (Acme CTO), Ben Cho (Acme SRE), Lina Park (Acme ML Eng), Tom Reynolds (Acme Procurement)
summary: Redwood product walkthrough focused on migrating from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together APIs to Redwood. Covered API parity (endpoints, function calling, streaming), embeddings mapping, cost/latency tradeoffs, hosted vs dedicated vs private, and security/compliance. Agreed to share parity spreadsheet, run benchmarks on Acme sample prompts, and follow up with pricing and security docs.
topics: API parity mapping (endpoints, params, response shapes)
function / tool calling differences and examples
latency vs cost (batching, KV cache, quantization)
Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private deployment tradeoffs
Security: SOC2, SAML/SSO, KMS, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, we'll run through the migration parity demo today, I think we have about 45 minutes, please interrupt.
[00:18] Sara (Acme CTO): Thanks Jordan, we mainly want to make sure parity with our current OpenAI/Anthropic/Together calls, and understand any edge case, like function calling and streaming.
[00:34] Priya (Redwood SE): Awesome, I'll share my screen in a sec - quick agenda: API surface, embeddings, streaming, routing and deployment options, then q&a and next steps.
[00:52] Ben (Acme SRE): Quick network note - we need to know IPs for allow-listing for hosted, and what's required for VPC with private.
[01:07] Jordan: Yup we'll cover that, and we'll also include the dedicated/private checklist in the follow up.
[01:25] Priya: So first, request/response parity: Redwood's text-generation endpoint accepts text or messages similar to the others, param names are slightly different - e.g., model, max_tokens, temperature, but we have a 1:1 mapping doc.
[01:45] Lina (ML Eng): Are there any differences in tokenization - like our analytics depend on token counts matching OpenAI's?
[02:00] Priya: Good question, Redwood exposes token counts in the response and uses compatible tokenizers for the common open models; there's sometimes small differences with Anthropic tokens, we'll call that out in the mapping sheet.
[02:18] Jordan: I'll add a note: tokenization fidelity varies by model family, we recommend running a small sample to validate.
[02:30] Alex (Product): Also note we support model aliases, so you can point existing code at a Redwood alias that routes to the most compatible variant. Helps with zero-change migration.
[02:50] Sara: Function calling - Together and Anthropic have slightly different patterns, how does Redwood handle that?
[03:03] Priya: Redwood supports both structured function calls and a generic tool-calling pattern. We map OpenAI-style function_call and Anthropic system-tool hints to our function schema; sample payloads in the spreadsheet. Example: you can register functions with types and Redwood will return a function_call object similar to OpenAI.
[03:25] Jordan: sometimes the auto-transcription here says "function call" wrong, but, uh, we include examples for nested args as well.
[03:40] Ben: And streaming? We rely on streaming for UI latency.
[03:48] Priya: We support streaming responses via SSE/websocket. The chunks include partial tokens, deltas, and we also surface finish_reason. One caveat: we recommend enabling prefix/KV cache for sessiony workloads to reduce cold-latency.
[04:06] Lina: KV cache - how is that surfaced? Is it automatic?
[04:14] Priya: It's automatic on compatible models; you can also programmatically pin prefixes. In Redwood docs we call it KV cache - sometimes transcribed as K.V. cash - ha.
[04:28] Sara: Embeddings - we use Together embeddings in prod, dimensions are 1536, will we get exact parity?
[04:38] Priya: We offer embeddings with dimensional parity for common model sizes; for open variants we list dims in the catalog. If there's a small mismatch we can provide mapping/transformation guidance.
[04:56] Jordan: cost discussion - Redwood will show per-token cost and per-embedding unit. For dedicated you get committed throughput and better unit economics.
[05:10] Tom (Procurement): On pricing, we need hosted per-token, dedicated monthly commit, and private licensing.
[05:19] Jordan: We'll include a pricing sheet. Also, Redwood Optimize gives recommendations that can lower cost by batching and quantization.
[05:33] Ben: Quantization - do you run that on inference runtime or do we need quantized models pre-loaded?
[05:40] Priya: Runtime supports quantization-friendly kernels; we offer curated quantized model variants so you don't have to re-quantize. It affects latency and perf per model, we can show numbers in the benchmark.
[05:58] Sara: Security: we need SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs, and data residency options - do you support HSM/KMS integrations?
[06:12] Jordan: Yes SOC2, SAML SSO, RBAC, MFA, audit logs. For keys we integrate with AWS KMS and customers can bring their own KMS/HSM in Private deployments. We'll attach the security pack.
[06:30] Priya: Also note that Dedicated runs in our tenancy and provides tenant isolation and private networking. Private gives you a customer-managed control plane.
[06:46] Lina: Latency numbers - what's typical p95 for generation for our 1k token bursts?
[06:55] Priya: It depends on model family and batch tuning. For high-throughput we hit mid 100s ms for 256 token workflows on optimized configs; for 1k tokens it's higher, obviously. We'll run your sample prompts to get concrete numbers.
[07:14] Jordan: We'll propose a pilot: Redwood runs the benchmark on your sample dataset, compare latency and cost vs OpenAI/Anthropic/Together.
[07:23] Ben: Network/setup - for private deployment, what's the onboarding timeline?
[07:30] Alex: Private onboarding is ~8-12 weeks typically, Dedicated is faster 2-6 weeks depending on capacity and contracts. Hosted is immediate.
[07:44] Sara: Are there any known breaking changes we should test for around truncation/stop sequences?
[07:52] Priya: Stop sequences are supported; minor differences in handling of multi-token stops happen based on tokenizer; we'll call those out in the mapping sheet.
[08:05] Tom: Compliance team will need a short statement about data retention and log redaction.
[08:11] Jordan: We'll include a short data retention whitepaper with redaction controls.
[08:20] Priya: Now I'll walk through a live mapping example: starting from OpenAI chat completion shape, this is a typical call...
[08:32] [screen share noise]
[08:40] Priya: Example 1: OpenAI chat -> messages param: history array, role/content. Redwood expects messages too, and model alias. Example curl posted in chat.
[08:55] Sara: Can you show an Anthropic example too?
[09:00] Priya: Sure - Anthropic has 'messages' with 'speaker' names; we translate that into Redwood messages on ingest, so your higher-level code can remain the same.
[09:15] Lina: What about Together's batching endpoint - we send batched prompts in single call, we need to preserve request ids in responses.
[09:25] Priya: Redwood supports batched requests and echoes request ids; we keep alignment and provide per-item token accounting.
[09:38] Jordan: I'm sharing a link to the parity spreadsheet in the chat: https://redwood.app/share/parity-acme-2026 - that'll have side-by-side request/response examples.
[09:55] Sara: Great. Regarding embeddings similarity, will we need to re-index?
[10:02] Priya: If dimensionality or base model differs, re-indexing is recommended. For same-dim variants, you can reuse indexes but we recommend validating.
[10:16] Ben: Benchmarks - we want 99th-pct latency, not just avg.
[10:22] Priya: Yep we report p50/p95/p99 and tail latencies in the benchmark artifacts.
[10:34] Jordan: For cost modeling, Redwood Optimize will suggest batching, cache TTLs, and quantization to hit cost targets; we'll include an initial config suggestion.
[10:45] [interruption noise]
[11:00] Tom: Legal process - we'll need contract template and DPA.
[11:07] Jordan: We'll share contract templates and DPA. Our sales operations will follow up.
[11:18] Sara: Any gotchas on rate limits when migrating? We use aggressive concurrent calls.
[11:26] Priya: Rate limits are configurable per account and per-route; for high concurrency we recommend Dedicated with autoscale/burst. We'll show a sample rate limit config.
[11:40] Lina: Tooling: will your SDKs support drop-in replacement?
[11:46] Alex: We provide lightweight SDKs and HTTP compatibility layers to reduce code changes - aliases help too.
[11:55] Ben: Observability - can we get token-level cost breakdown in console?
[12:01] Jordan: Yes Redwood Console has token-level cost, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks and error analysis. We'll share screenshots.
[12:12] Priya: Quick demo: here's an example of function call going to a registered tool, how Redwood returns the call payload and how you execute handlers.
[12:29] [typing sounds]
[12:38] Priya: Important: for nested function args we preserve JSON schema; sometimes transcriptions call this out wrong.
[12:49] Sara: For the benchmark, we'll measure both p95 and cost per 1M tokens, can you include embedding throughput too?
[12:58] Priya: Yes embedding throughput and per-embedding cost included.
[13:08] Jordan: Notes on fallbacks - Redwood can route to cheaper model variants automatically on overload; you can set quality SLOs and fallback policies.
[13:20] Ben: If we route across regions for latency, does observability still show global traces?
[13:27] Alex: Yes Console consolidates traces across routes and regions.
[13:35] Tom: Procurement question: can dedicated capacity be reserved monthly, and what's cancellation terms?
[13:42] Jordan: We'll share the reserved capacity contract summary in follow-up.
[13:50] Sara: Any customers migrated from Anthropic who saw subtle behavior changes?
[13:58] Priya: A few customers saw small prompt tuning differences; we helped with prompt adapters and model aliasing. We'll provide a case note.
[14:12] [brief pause]
[14:30] Priya: Ok, quick live demo of a streaming call - you can see token deltas come in and we surface partials; then we show finish_reason.
[14:45] [demo audio]
[15:05] Jordan: To wrap, our proposed pilot: 1) Acme provides 5k sample prompts and traffic profile, 2) Redwood runs benchmark on hosted or dedicated (you choose), 3) we produce latency/cost report + recommended config + mapping sheet.
[15:24] Sara: Timeline - we want results within two weeks of sample submission. Is that doable?
[15:31] Priya: Yes for hosted we can usually run quick comparisons within 7-10 business days; dedicated/private take longer because of infra.
[15:41] Ben: We'll need to schedule the technical deep dive for infra specifics.
[15:46] Jordan: Priya will lead the deep dive and I'll coordinate contract/pricing.
[15:54] Tom: Ok from procurement perspective we'll prepare initial questions and schedule a follow-up.
[16:00] Jordan: Great, I'll follow up with the parity spreadsheet, pricing doc, security pack, and a calendar invite for the deep dive.
[16:11] Sara: Thanks all, this was helpful.
[16:15] Priya: Thanks, we'll get those artifacts over.
[16:20] [call ends]
